observations: Codex first model probe discovered MCP but required tool approval. Setting default_tools_approval_mode=approve only for the turn-scoped app MCP server fixed execution while the sandbox remained read-only and approvalPolicy never.

Codex live search required both the provider supports_standalone_web_search capability and features.standalone_web_search. The final turn emitted web_search and read_page events and answered from the real page.

features.skills is ignored by this installed CLI. Tools-on adds skills.include_instructions=false, skills.bundled.enabled=false and features.skill_search=false. The final native rollout contains no skills instructions block. Tools-off retains its old launch arguments.

Codex native tokenUsage totals and last-call breakdowns were inspected across three model calls; the final adapter usage includes every call with cached reads separated. Resumed-turn usage excludes prior-turn totals.

Both native CLIs resumed their saved session with a new MCP connection and successfully ran the app tool. Token rotation/revocation, Stop, failure, concurrent isolation and reply persistence are additionally covered by the protocol and SDK client tests.
Native Codex webSearch events report action metadata when the CLI omits raw search results; no missing result text is invented.
